newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIA'S CONGRESS GATHERS TO REVIVE FORTUNES.
newsitem.headline: INDIA'S CONGRESS GATHERS TO REVIVE FORTUNES.

text.p: India's ailing Congress party, the nation's oldest political grouping, starts a three-day meeting on Friday which leaders said will reinvigorate the party after a humiliating electoral defeat last year.
"The plenary session will help to revive the Congress," general secretary Ghulam Nabi Azad told Reuters.
The 112-year-old party, once the political umbrella for Mahatma Gandhi but trounced in general elections last year, holds its 80th plenary session in the eastern city of Calcutta.
The city wore a festive look. Large colourful cut-outs of Congress leaders and freedom fighters from the past lined the streets, while loudspeakers blared out patriotic songs.
Congress has ruled India for all but five years since independence from British rule in 1947, but has been repeatedly stung by scandal and was thrown out of power in last year's polls.
It now provides make-or-break support to Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's ruling United Front coalition but holds no government portfolios.
Congress leaders, some itching to return to power, reaffirmed their support for Gujral's minority government but said coalition politics had failed to provide the nation with stability.
"Coalition politics has not paid dividends," senior Congress leader Sharad Pawar told Reuters. "The people have come to realise that it is only Congress which can provide stability."
Pawar added: "But we will continue to support the Gujral government."
The party was set to adopt resolutions on political, economic and international issues.

Former finance minister Manmohan Singh, who spearheaded free-market reforms between 1991 and 1996, said the party would recommit itself to economic liberalisation but stressed that reforms must help ease poverty.
"The economic resolution will definitely be pro-poor," Azad said.
The Congress government headed by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1991 launched radical reforms by opening up trade and industry after decades of socialist controls.

The party will elect 10 members to its decision-making Congress Working Committee (CWC) at the plenary session, which was expected to be attended by Sonia Gandhi, the reclusive widow of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi.

Party president Sitaram Kesri, who was re-elected in June, plunged the 15-party United Front government into crisis in March by withdrawing his party's support, leading to the defeat of prime minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a parliamentary confidence vote on April 11.
The centre-left United Front alliance then chose Gujral as its leader and won back Congress support.
